panel.introduction: Calypso follows Tethys around Saturn, about 60° behind the larger moon. Its elongated shape carries overlapping craters and unusually smooth, bright surface deposits.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: Cassini clear-filter observations projected onto the released PDS shape using its measured camera geometry. Bounded illumination correction and exposure matching reduce photographed lighting. Gray grid marks unavailable samples; cast-shadow terrain is not reconstructed.
controls.title: ISS mosaic
controls.summary: Brightness matching reduces photographed shading. The gray grid marks missing coverage and terrain hidden in cast shadows.

controls.label: False color
controls.description: Cassini ISS NAC red, green and blue filters projected independently with the released PDS shape-camera table. Colors explicitly encode those three filters as red, green and blue; they are a registered false-color display, not natural color or a calibrated albedo map. Gray grid marks terrain outside the common reliable observation footprint and cast-shadow terrain is not reconstructed. Blue was captured almost nine minutes before red, at a phase angle of 43 degrees versus 33 degrees. Hue can reflect changing illumination as well as filter response; it does not establish composition.
controls.title: Cassini false color
controls.summary: False color from registered source filters. The images were taken minutes apart, so changing illumination also affects hue. Gray grid marks missing common coverage.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Radial height above a 10.7 km reference sphere from the Cassini shape model. Includes the moon’s broad irregular shape; it is not local height above a geoid. Fixed relief lighting reveals model slopes. Small craters are not reliably resolved.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
controls.summary: Height relative to a 10.7 km sphere, from the Cassini shape model. Small craters are unresolved.
